The "'''spacefaring benefactors'''" were a mysterious group who relocated seventeen sentient [[Water/Legends|aquatic]] [[Species/Legends|species]] to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Iskalon/Legends|Iskalon]] from their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworlds]] which faced a series of cataclysms.<ref name="Gamer1" /> approximately five [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]] before the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="Date">{{CSWECite|II|119|Iskalonian}} states that the [[Species/Legends|species]] constituting the [[Iskalonian]] cultural group were brought to [[Iskalon/Legends|Iskalon]] approximately five [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]] before the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Since {{GamerCite|1|The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Marvel Series}} establishes that the Iskalonian [[Species/Legends|species]] were relocated by a group of [[Realspace/Legends|spacefaring]] benefactors, the group must have also existed by that [[Time/Legends|time]].</ref> Their relocating of aquatic species led to the creation of the [[Iskalonian]] society, an example of cultural fusion.<ref name="Gamer1" />

The benefactors' identity remained a mystery at least until the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], when the [[Shi'ido]] anthropologist [[Mammon Hoole]] led an expedition to the ruins of the seventeen species, in hopes of discovering the nature of the cataclysms and the identity of the benevolent spacers.<ref name="Gamer1" />

==Behind the scenes==
The spacefaring benefactors were mentioned in "[[The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Marvel Series]]," an article published in the [[Star Wars Gamer 1|first issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' magazine. They fit the stereotype of the "ancient vanished precursors", but their relations to the [[Celestial/Legends|Celestials]] or the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]], if any, have never been revealed.
